h1: The 7 Best Roku TVs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best Roku TVs of 2026, from a 32 inch Hisense to 75 inch Mini-LED models, with picks by room size and budget.
summary: The Roku 55 inch Select Series QLED is the best overall for most living rooms. The 65 inch Plus Series Mini-LED is the step up for bright rooms, the 75 inch Pro is for big spaces, the Westinghouse 50 is a budget 4K choice, and the Hisense 32 QLED and Roku 40 suit bedrooms and desks.
intro: The easiest Roku TV mistake is buying size first and panel second. A 65 inch screen with a basic panel can look worse in a bright room than a 55 inch QLED, because brightness and contrast are what make a picture pop, not diagonal inches. Think about the room before the screen size.

We reviewed seven Roku powered TVs on paper, comparing screen size, panel type and resolution from the listings. We left out the Roku Ultra, which is a streaming player, not a TV. Specs here are thin, so we say where details are missing.

products.name: Roku 55-Inch Select Series Smart TV 2026-4K QLED TV - Roku TV
products.verdict: A 55 inch 4K QLED that fits most living rooms.
products.description:
This Roku Select Series is a 55 inch 4K QLED smart TV in the $200 to $500 tier. QLED uses a quantum dot layer to widen the color range over a standard LED panel.

It ranks first because it combines 4K, QLED and a mid size screen at a moderate price. The step up to the 65 inch Plus gives Mini-LED and more size, but costs more.

Buy it for a typical living room or large bedroom. Details on brightness and refresh rate are not listed, so check them before deciding.
products.skipIf: You want a very large screen.

products.name: Roku 65-Inch Plus Series Smart TV - 4K QLED Mini-LED TV - RokuTV
products.verdict: More size and a Mini-LED backlight.
products.description:
The Plus Series is a 65 inch 4K QLED Mini-LED TV in the $200 to $500 tier. Mini-LED uses a denser backlight, which helps contrast and brightness.

It ranks second because it adds Mini-LED and ten inches over the Select, at a similar price tier. The tradeoff is room: a 65 inch screen needs a wide wall.

Choose it for a bright living room. Check the stand width against your furniture.

products.name: Roku 75-Inch Pro Series Smart TV - 4K QLED Mini-LED TV - RokuTV
products.verdict: A 75 inch Mini-LED for big rooms.
products.description:
The Pro Series is a 75 inch 4K QLED Mini-LED TV in the $500 and up tier.

It ranks third because it costs the most and only suits large rooms. The Plus above gives similar tech at 65 inches for less.

Buy it if you sit far from the screen. Sitting close to 75 inches tires the eyes.

products.name: Westinghouse Roku TV - 50 Inch Smart TV
products.verdict: A 50 inch 4K Roku TV at a modest price.
products.description:
This Westinghouse is a 50 inch 4K smart TV with Roku built in, in the $200 to $500 tier. The listing gives no panel type.

It ranks below the Roku Select because the Select adds a QLED panel. This one is the simpler choice.

Pick it for a guest room or secondary TV where color depth matters less.

products.name: Roku Smart TV - 43-Inch Select Series 4K HDR RokuTV with Roku
products.verdict: A small 4K HDR set for bedrooms.
products.description:
The 43 inch Select Series is a 4K HDR Roku TV. No price tier was available for this one.

It ranks fifth because it is 4K at a compact size, unlike the 40 inch below, which is 1080p. The tradeoff is no QLED panel.

Choose it for a bedroom or small apartment where space is limited.

products.name: Hisense 32-Inch Class QD4SR Series Hi-QLED HD Smart Roku TV (32QD4HSR
products.verdict: A 32 inch QLED that works on a desk.
products.description:
The Hisense QD4SR is a 32 inch Hi-QLED HD smart Roku TV in the $100 to $200 tier. HD means 720p or 1080p, below 4K.

It ranks sixth because the screen is small, but QLED at 32 inches is unusual and it fits desks and kitchens.

Buy it for a dorm, kitchen or desk.

products.name: Roku 40-Inch Select Series Smart TV 2026-1080p Full HD TV - RokuTV
products.verdict: A 40 inch 1080p set for small rooms.
products.description:
This is a 40 inch 1080p Full HD Roku TV in the $100 to $200 tier.

It ranks last because 1080p at 40 inches trails the 4K 43 inch model, and it offers no HDR or QLED in the listing.

Choose it for a small bedroom TV on a tight budget.

whatMatters.detail: A common rule is to sit about 1.5 times the diagonal away for 4K. A 65 inch TV suits roughly 8 feet. Measure your seating distance and wall width first.
4K has four times the pixels of 1080p. It matters most on screens above 43 inches. Look for 4K in the title.
QLED adds a quantum dot layer for richer color. It improves vividness over basic LED. Check the panel type in the title.
Mini-LED uses many tiny backlights for better contrast. It helps in bright rooms. Look for Mini-LED in the title.
Roku TV puts all streaming apps on one home screen. It saves buying a separate stick. Confirm Roku in the name.

faq.q: Do all of these use Roku?
faq.a: Yes, every TV here runs the Roku platform built in, so no stick is needed.
Buying by size only. Panel type matters in bright rooms.

faq.q: Is Mini-LED worth it over QLED?
faq.a: In bright rooms, yes. The Roku 65 Plus adds it at a similar price tier to the 55 Select.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Connect to Wi-Fi, sign in to Roku and add your apps.

faq.q: Do I need a Roku Ultra?
faq.a: No. The Ultra is a streaming player, so these TVs do not need it.
At 40 inches or less, yes. Above that, choose 4K.

finalTake: The Roku 55 Select QLED is the best buy for most homes, with the 65 Plus Mini-LED for bright rooms. Use the Westinghouse for a cheap 4K, and the Hisense 32 or Roku 40 for small spaces. Pick size by distance, then panel.
